manifest.example:
# The app's operational contract (docs/app-contract.md, schemas/company-app.schema.json).
# ihc-app provision reads it on every push to main.
schema_version: 1

app:
  slug: purchase-requests
  name: Purchase requests
  owner_email: ana@example.com
  description: Internal app built on the company cloud.

runtime:
  type: docker-compose
  compose_file: docker-compose.yml
  service: app
  port: 8080
  healthcheck:
    type: http
    path: /health
    expected_status: 200

deploy:
  enabled: true
  domain: purchase-requests.cloud.example.com
  port: auto
  env_example: .env.example

auth:
  required: true
  provider: forward-auth

database:
  required: true
  engine: postgres

dependencies:
  redis:
    required: true

# Files (uploads, exports): set true for a bucket of the app's own on the shared S3 storage
# (the cloud's storage profile must be on). The deploy writes S3_ENDPOINT, S3_BUCKET,
# S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID, S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, S3_REGION into the app's env (README.md, "Files").
object_storage:
  required: false

# Tools for AI agents through the cloud's MCP gateway (docs/app-contract.md, "MCP"). The
# gateway lists GET tools_path and calls POST execute_path on this app's container with an
# actor JWT (aud = audience, scope = the scopes below granted to the caller's groups);
# server.js checks it. In the gateway the tools are named <slug>__<tool>. Delete the
# section to keep the app out of the gateway.
mcp:
  audience: purchase-requests.mcp
  tools_path: /mcp/tools
  execute_path: /mcp/tools/{tool}/execute
  scopes:
    purchase-requests.read:
      - ihc-users

checks:
  build_command: docker compose build
  test_command: npm test

provided.name: DATABASE_URL
provided.meaning: the app's own Postgres database, created empty

auth.notes: The proxy signs the person in; the app reads who it is from the header.

rules.text: No host network, PID, IPC or user namespace.
No Postgres, Redis or S3 server in the compose file; use DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL, S3_*.
